report.ph: What was being done and what went wrong (may be left empty)
report.copied: Report copied — paste it into a chat or email

report.caption: Melete problem report

mesh.title: Devices
mesh.qrHint: On another Melete device: “Connect a device” — point the camera at the code.
mesh.hint: Same Wi-Fi network. Songs, sessions, calendar, reading and media files sync both ways without duplicates. The link is secured: a device remembers the other one’s fingerprint when connecting.
mesh.hintPc: A phone with Melete DEV: “Accept connections” — enter its address and code here. Then sync and remote control of the phone from the computer.
net.sendHint: “{name}” will appear in the media library of the chosen device.
rc.title: Remote: {name}
rc.none: Nothing is playing — pick a recording below.
rc.err.net: The device does not answer: same Wi-Fi, Melete open, accepting connections.
rc.err.key: The device forgot this one — connect again.
rc.err.off: The media library did not open on the device.
rc.toolsHint: The instrument opens on that device — play it there.
sy.pcHint: Songs, sessions, calendar, reading and recordings are synced; the computer processes the phone’s recordings itself — stems, lyrics, key and chords go back. Settings stay per device.
ens.title: Ensemble
ens.failed: Could not assemble — details in the log
ens.done: Done — aligned tracks are in the library; in the looper use “+” → “Recording from the library” or “Project from the old studio”.
ens.cleanDone: Clean tracks — as a second project.
ens.hostOff: Phones connect through the phone link. It is off.
ens.hostHint: On the phones: “Settings → Data → Computer link” (address {addr}, code {code}), then “Ensemble”.
ens.cleanHint: Only its own part from each recording. Long processing, separate project
ens.hostFtr: Before the count-in and after “Stop” the computer plays a short signal; tracks are aligned by it to a fraction of a millisecond, with clock drift corrected. Computer in the middle of the room, volume up. Originals stay on the phones.
ens.err.send: Recording saved in the media library, but not sent
ens.err.hostoff: Ensemble is not open on the computer
ens.sent: Sent. Waiting for the next take
ens.waitStart: Waiting for the computer to start recording
ens.phoneFtr: Phone next to its instrument. The recording is saved in the media library and sent to the computer automatically.
sy.what: Songs, sessions, calendar, reading, recordings with stems, notes and lyrics — both ways; deletions carry over. Settings stay per device.
sy.pcWorkHint: The computer splits stems and finds lyrics, key and chords of new recordings, saving the phone’s battery; results arrive on their own when it is quiet and the computer is nearby. No computer for over a day — the phone does it itself.
sy.err.busy: Music is playing on the computer — syncing later
gs.title: Share on the network
gs.openHint: Anyone on this Wi-Fi opens the address in a browser and sees the songs.
gs.closedHint: Only via the QR code on this screen, with approval here.
gs.noSets: No set lists — they are made in the calendar.
gs.audioHint: guests listen one song at a time; the file does not stay with them
gs.addr: address for a browser, or the QR code
gs.qrOnly: access only via the QR code
gs.hint: Guests on the same Wi-Fi see lyrics, chords and the set list and listen to recordings — read only. When the leader opens a song, it opens for guests who follow. Sessions, stats and personal data are not shared.
sy.done: Done: songs +{songs}, sessions +{sessions}, files to computer {up}, from computer {down}
sy.err.addr: That does not look like the computer’s address
sy.err.unreachable: The computer does not answer: same Wi-Fi? Is “Accept the phone” on?
sy.err.code: Wrong code — check the computer screen
sy.err.wait: Too many wrong codes — wait a minute
sy.err.off: “Accept the phone” is off on the computer
sy.err.key: The computer forgot this phone — connect again
sy.err.pin: A different computer is answering (or Melete was reinstalled on it) — connect again
sy.err.repair: The connection is now encrypted — connect the phone again: the code is on the computer screen
sy.err.tls: The computer does not accept the secure connection — update Melete on the computer
sy.err.port: Could not turn on: the port is busy
sy.err.port2: Port busy: another Melete (DEV or regular) is open with “Accept phone” on. Close it and turn this on again.
check.title: Self-check
check.sub: sound, recording, storage, models — on this device
check.intro: The app checks its own sound, audio clock, player, microphone, recording, storage, models and screen. A short quiet tone will play. The result goes to the log and the problem report; nothing is sent.
diag.title: Diagnostics
diag.sub: how the app runs on this device — counted by itself
diag.intro: The app tracks sound, speed and errors by itself. Data stays on the device.
diag.noCheck: Self-check has not been run yet
diag.report: Send a report with the summary
diag.clearAsk: Diagnostic counters start over. The log and data stay.
diag.privacy: Technical data only: no song or file names, texts, name, sound or frames.
diag.f.overload: Audio could not keep up: {min90} min above 90 %
diag.h.overload: Eco sound mode (Settings → Sound) or fewer tools open at once helps.
diag.h.overloadAt: Mostly with: {when}. Eco sound mode (Settings → Sound) or fewer tools open at once helps.
diag.f.squeeze: Voices were cut under load {n} times
diag.h.squeeze: The app reduced voices to avoid crackling. If the sound gets thin — eco mode or fewer pads.
diag.h.underrun: The audio thread skipped blocks — these are clicks. A larger buffer (Settings → Sound → Smooth) usually fixes it.
diag.h.latency: High for live playing. The Fast buffer in sound settings lowers it if the processor copes.
diag.h.latencyOut: Almost all of the latency is in the phone output (Bluetooth headphones or speaker); the app buffer is already small. Wired headphones or USB audio are fastest.
diag.f.late: The studio was late with notes {n} times (up to {ms} ms)
diag.h.late: The main thread was busy. Close extra windows; if it repeats — send a report.
diag.f.freeze: The interface froze {n} times, up to {max} ms
diag.h.freeze: Touches and sound lag at those moments. A report will show where.
diag.h.crash: A problem report with the log helps find the cause.
diag.h.start: Slow. A report will show what holds the start.
diag.f.modload: Tools take up to {s} s to open
diag.h.modload: The first open is slower (loading); if every time — send a report.
diag.h.stems: Heavy for this device: compute while charging or on the computer (“Compute on the computer”).
diag.h.ana: Normal for a slow device: it runs in the background, in silence.
diag.f.render: Studio mixdown is only {x}× faster than real time
diag.h.render: A heavy project for this device. Mix down on the computer or simplify effects.
diag.h.memory: Risk of being closed by the system. Close large PDFs and recordings not needed now.
diag.h.disk: Too little for recordings and processing. Free up space on the device.
diag.h.check: Open the self-check — each row says what is wrong.
diag.h.nocheck: Run it — about half a minute.
diag.f.bench: Low audio headroom: {x}× faster than real time
diag.h.bench: Crackling is possible under load. Eco sound mode and light reverb give headroom.

lic.snd.title: Sounds and graphics
lic.snd.text: All app sounds (metronome, piano, drone, pads, clicks) are synthesized in real time and use no third-party recordings; tabs and the studio's General MIDI sounds use the SONiVOX bank listed above. Icons and illustrations were drawn for the app. Music theory facts (scales, chords, tunings, tempo names) are common knowledge.
tos.title: Before you start
tos.p1: The app is free and has no ads. Microphone sound is processed on the device only and is never sent anywhere.
tos.p2: Everything you add yourself — recordings, tabs, lyrics — stays on your device and is your responsibility. Only add things you have the rights to.

me.hint: Experience before the app is just for reference: it counts toward neither the league nor the statistics. Profile data is stored only on this device.
ob.intro: A few steps to set up the app: instruments, level, experience and a weekly goal.
ob.importHint: Songs, quote collections and a profile — from a team file or one built by an AI using the instructions. After loading, the next steps are already filled in.
ob.name: Name
ob.private: No account needed: all answers are stored on this device only and can be changed in the profile.
ob.instText: You can pick several. The tuner’s tuning depends on this.
ob.levelText: A rough estimate. For beginners the tuner and glider are set up more simply.
level.beginner.text: The first months of practice. The tuner shows the strings, the glider plays notes only.
level.amateur.text: The basics are familiar, playing for yourself.
level.pro.text: Music is the main occupation: performing, teaching, recording.
ob.expText: Roughly how many hours are already behind — just for reference. Only hours played in the app count toward the league and the statistics.
ob.goalText: Progress is counted by weeks: the total hours matter, not daily streaks.
ob.goalHint: The goal is suggested by level and can be changed at any time.
lic.cg.sub: Font of the note on the glider board
lic.cg.text: Distributed under the SIL Open Font License 1.1 (openfontlicense.org), like the Bravura font above. Used without changes.
idle.watchTitle: The stopwatch is running. Is the practice still going?
idle.textQuiet: No sound and no actions for 10 minutes.
idle.wait: Without an answer within 5 minutes, tracking stops; time after the last action is not counted.
idle.ended: Session ended due to inactivity. Counted {d}, up to the last action.
idle.ended0: Session ended due to inactivity. Less than a minute was not counted.
idle.watchHidden: Stopwatch stopped: the app was in the background with no sound.
presence.title: Confirm playing by sound
presence.hint: The microphone measures loudness only; nothing is recorded. 10 minutes without playing or actions ends the session.
auto.title: Media library
auto.stemsHintPhone: Each recording is split into vocals and instrumental in the background, newest first. 4 and 6 stems, chords and notes are done by the computer (phone link).
auto.stemsHintDev: Every media library recording is split into stems in the background, newest first. 4 and 6 stems need the “Full separation” pack (Modules and features → Packs); slow on a phone.
auto.hqHintDev: Vocals by Mel-RoFormer (“Better vocals” pack), the rest by HTDemucs in three passes. Very slow on a phone; better while charging. Without the pack — several passes of the usual models.
auto.stemsHint: Every library recording is separated into stems in the background, most recent first. 2 — vocals and instrumental, 4 — plus drums and bass, 6 — plus guitar and keys. Results are in the player: each stem's volume along with key and speed.
auto.hqHint: Two passes instead of one: cleaner vocals, twice the time. All recordings get the normal split first, then finished ones are redone. The first version stays — the player can switch back to it.
auto.powerHint: Separation runs only in silence — when nothing is playing. “While charging” — only while the device charges, usually overnight: 10–20 songs per night. “Always” — on battery too, until everything is done.
auto.anaHint: Every new recording gets its key, tempo, beats and chords — shown in the library and the player. The web version detects only key and tempo.
presence.bt: Bluetooth headphones: the mic stays off so the sound does not drop to call quality.
presence.denied: No microphone access — confirming playing by sound is off.
presence.unavailable: Microphone unavailable — confirming playing by sound is off.
nosnd.mixer: Sound is off in the mixer: {bus}
idle.neverDone: Questions are off. Time without actions is not counted. They can be turned back on in App prompts.
share.title: Send to the team
share.setSend: Send to the team with songs
share.hint: Sent: song, key, tempo, lyrics with chords, metronome. Kept: progress, difficulty, current tempo, tags, practice time.
share.notMelete: This is not a Melete file
share.newer: The file comes from a newer Melete — an update is needed
share.exists: Already here — will be updated (mastery and practice time are kept)
share.inHint: Tabs, scores and recordings from the file go to the media library and are linked to the songs; identical files are not duplicated.
share.about: Songs with lyrics, chords and tabs — in one file. A set list — from a calendar event. No servers or sign-up.
rem.classicHint: Before practice: an hour ahead — “practice today”, 5 minutes ahead — “time to get the instrument out”. When to remind is chosen below.
rem.pushyHint: All day, 6–8 times: morning, before lunch, afternoon, before dinner, an hour and 5 minutes before practice and after. Clingy until practice happens.
ob.meleteText: Melete is the mascot: reminds about practice and says one word a day. Character, time and words can be changed in settings.
rem.quietHint: No notifications at all. Melete stays calm on the home screen; the word of the day remains.
rem.byNameHint: “Alex, practice today…” — the name from the profile
rem.customHint: Own schedule: any reminders (up to 10 a day) — before practice, after or at an exact time, each in its own style.
rem.title: Practice reminders
rem.testSent: Reminder shown — it is in the notification shade
rem.denied: Notifications are blocked — they can be allowed in the phone settings
rem.testOff: Reminders are off — choose a character first
rem.testFail: Could not show the notification — details are in the log (Profile → Report a problem)
rem.exactHint: The phone may currently shift reminders by a few minutes. Tap to allow “Alarms & reminders”
rem.autoHint: On Honor, Huawei, Xiaomi and others reminders do not arrive while the app is closed without it. Tap to allow launch and background work
rem.nextNone: No reminders scheduled — open the app or check permissions
rem.hint: Only on practice days; none after practice that day. Silence from {from}:00 to {to}:00.
rem.webOnly: Reminders arrive in the Android app.

church.title: Church mode
church.hint: The Bible (Russian Synodal translation, 66 books) and daily readings by plan — on the home screen and in the calendar.
church.hintOn: The Bible is in the tools; the daily reading is on the home screen and in the calendar. The rhythm is weekly: nothing missed burns.
plan.year: The whole Bible in a year
plan.yearpar: Old and New Testament in parallel, in a year
plan.psprov: Psalms and Proverbs in a month
bplan.title: Own reading plan
bplan.name: Name
bplan.hint: Chapters of the chosen books go in order, evenly across the days. A missed day does not burn — readings wait.
feat.toolsOnly.hint: Only tools, songs and calendar — no time tracking, stats, leagues or notifications. Recorded data is kept.
find.note: Searches by title and artist in the open MusicBrainz database (musicbrainz.org). Only the query text is sent, and only when the button is pressed.
find.need: Enter a title or an artist first.
find.err.busy: The MusicBrainz database is busy. Try again in a few seconds.
find.none: Nothing found. Refine the title or add the artist.
an.title: Tempo and key from a recording
an.note: Analysis runs on the device. The result is approximate: tempo may be doubled or halved, the key a neighbouring one.
an.format: This file format is not supported.
an.fail: The recording could not be analysed.
an.done: Detected from the recording: {r}. The values are filled into “Target” and “Key”.
an.weak: Low confidence — best to check by ear.

hc.start.name: How Melete works
hc.start.what: A practice journal and musician’s tools. Data stays on this device.
hc.start.1: “Practice” — the week, goal and league; “Start practice” — a session with tools.
hc.start.3: Profile (top left) — goal, reminders, appearance, data.
hc.start.tip: The rhythm is weekly: a missed day resets nothing.
hc.songs.name: Songs
hc.songs.what: Everything for learning a song — in one card.
hc.songs.1: “+” — a song: key, tempo, lyrics with chords ([Am] before a syllable).
hc.songs.2: The card holds time, tempo chart and files; “Play” starts a session with the song.

wel.title: Melete — a musician’s companion
wel.p1: Melete helps to practise music regularly and calmly: practice tracking, songs and a calendar, a metronome, a tuner and other tools — in one app. The rhythm is weekly, with no pressure of daily streaks.
wel.p2: The app was created with Claude Code. It is completely free and open: the source code is distributed under the GPL-3.0 licence. No ads, subscriptions, accounts or data collection — everything stays on the device.
wel.p3: Melete was made for one purpose — to benefit musicians and to serve the good.
wel.legal: The app is provided “as is”, without warranties of any kind. To the extent permitted by applicable law, the developer is not responsible for how the app is used or for the materials added to it.
wel.accept: Tapping “Start” means agreement with the Terms of Use and the Privacy Policy.

snd.engineHint: “New” computes pads, worship keys, glider and theremin in one node per note — three times cheaper for the CPU. Applies to new notes.
snd.verbHint: “Light” is an algorithm like in phone synthesizers: tens of times cheaper for the processor. “Convolution” is more precise, but with all instruments at once the audio thread may fall behind. Light by default on a phone. Applies immediately.
snd.algoHint: Melete — own spaces, default and in eco mode. Galactic — a vast floating space for pads; Verbity — a dense natural hall (Airwindows): slightly more load, idle in silence.
snd.loadHint: Share of time the audio thread spends computing: up to 70 % there is headroom, from 90 % dropouts are likely (fewer voices or “Lite” quality). The same meter is in the mixer drawer.
